# Hunt checklist — PHP2Shell (PHP unauthenticated RCE, CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619)

Work top to bottom. Check the box when done, note what you found.
Detection and forensic triage only — do not attempt to reproduce the flaw or run exploit code.

## 1. Am I even in scope?
- [ ] Is this host running PHP that serves web requests? Confirm version and
      SAPI on every host: `php -v`, plus the web server configuration
      (Apache mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed/LSAPI).
- [ ] Severity: CVSS 3.1 **9.8** (CVE-2026-109618) / **8.1** (CVE-2026-109619);
      CVSS 4.0 **9.2** for both (PHP security team). Both are unauthenticated
      remote code execution as the web worker account.
- [ ] Affected: every supported branch below the fixed builds — **8.2.35**,
      **8.3.36**, **8.4.27**, **8.5.12** (GHSA ranges: < 8.2.35, < 8.3.36,
      < 8.4.27, < 8.5.12). PHP 8.1 and older get no official fix; CISA says
      take those systems offline until they can be patched or updated.
- [ ] SAPI risk is not equal: Apache mod_php is the highest-risk SAPI (RCE
      confirmed over HTTP, before any application code runs). PHP-FPM is
      susceptible too (no complete FPM exploit demonstrated for CVE-2026-109618;
      the session-lifecycle path for CVE-2026-109619 was validated against
      FPM). FrankenPHP is likely susceptible; LSAPI is conditional.
- [ ] Already on a patched build → still do §5 if the host ran unpatched
      while internet-exposed. Patching does not remove a planted shell.

## 2. What there is no signature for (read first)
- [ ] The flaw is memory corruption inside PHP itself, reached before any
      application code runs. The triggering request has **no distinctive URI,
      header, or payload string** to hunt on the wire — do not spend the hunt
      looking for one.
- [ ] What the advisories document as trigger shapes (WAF-log review only, a
      weak signal): multipart requests whose decoded shape is far outside
      your baseline — a part carrying an unusually large number of headers,
      many empty file controls, deeply nested field names, or a body that
      keeps arriving after the declared content length is exhausted. These
      shapes can push a worker toward out-of-memory. Alone they prove nothing
      (legitimate uploads can be lumpy); they are worth correlating only with
      §3 signals or worker crashes in the same window.
- [ ] For CVE-2026-109619 the exploit needs **two requests on the same
      worker**: a producer that leaves stale state behind, and a consumer —
      a later request — that reads it before normal initialization. That is
      why single-request log review finds nothing. Hunt the worker's
      behaviour, not the request.

## 3. The post-trigger signals (detection)
- [ ] Process logs (Sysmon EventID 1 / auditd execve): a PHP web worker's
      child is a shell (`sh`, `bash`, `dash`, `zsh`) — the primary signal,
      CISA's stated observable ("PHP worker processes launching shells or
      downloading tools")
- [ ] Same source: a PHP worker's child — or a shell's child — is `curl` or
      `wget`
- [ ] Network (Sysmon EventID 3 / Zeek conn): the flagged shell or download
      tool connecting out
- [ ] File (Sysmon EventID 11 / auditd): a PHP worker creating a new
      `.php` / `.phtml` under the web root, uploads, or `/tmp` — excluding
      template-cache directories (`storage/framework/views`, `var/cache`,
      `cache/twig`), which frameworks write legitimately
- [ ] Worker health: FPM child exits, segfaults, `Allowed memory size
      exhausted` / OOM entries in the PHP error log, or worker restarts
      clustering around the same window. A crash alone is not exploitation;
      a crash next to the signals above is

## 4. Correlate
- [ ] Same host, within 60 minutes: SHELL_SPAWN + any other signal kind →
      incident
- [ ] SHELL_SPAWN alone → suspicious; triage the command line. Known
      application shell-outs (document conversion, media tools) are the main
      false-positive source — allowlist the exact command, never the signal
      class
- [ ] WEBSHELL_DROP alone → incident candidate; a planted shell survives
      patching, so this is a forensic-triage trigger even on a patched host
- [ ] TOOL_DOWNLOAD / NET_OUT alone → suspicious; check the destination (in
      the sample the destinations are documentation-range stand-ins; in real
      logs, an unfamiliar external IP)

## 5. Forensic triage (CISA KEV `forensicTriage: Yes`)
A host that ran unpatched PHP while internet-exposed must be checked for
compromise, not merely patched. CISA lists both CVEs with forensic triage
required; ransomware use is Unknown for both.

- [ ] New or unexpected `.php` under the web root, uploads, `/tmp`, or
      anywhere a web worker can write — treat as hostile until proven
      otherwise; compare content against known-good
- [ ] Unexpected processes running as the web worker account; unexpected
      outbound connections from the web server around the window
- [ ] Unexpected users, cron jobs, systemd units, or `authorized_keys` for
      the web worker account
- [ ] If anything above is unclean: isolate, rotate credentials (database,
      application secrets, hosting panel, SSO), restore from a known-good
      backup, then bring the patched build online. Patching alone does not
      remove a planted shell
- [ ] CISA: patch immediately, internet-facing systems first; PHP 8.1 and
      older → take offline until patched or updated

## 6. Hardening while you patch
- [ ] Update to **8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35** for your branch — the
      only complete mitigation, per both advisories
- [ ] Interim, per the advisories (partial, not complete): for
      CVE-2026-109618, `memory_limit=-1` removes the predictable per-request
      limit the confirmed exploit uses — but it is not complete, because an
      `mmap()` failure can still trigger the vulnerable path. Keep
      `post_max_size` conservative and enforce the decoded request size at
      the frontend; reduce `max_input_nesting_level`; bound input variables,
      multipart parts, headers per part, and uploads; block multipart at the
      frontend if the app does not use it. Do **not** use `RLIMIT_AS` /
      `RLIMIT_DATA` — they make `mmap()` fail and trigger the vulnerable path
- [ ] Interim, per the advisories (partial): for CVE-2026-109619,
      `session.upload_progress.enabled=0` kills the demonstrated
      session-lifecycle path, and on PHP 8.5 `fatal_error_backtraces=0`
      removes the producer behind the confirmed case; consider
      `pm.max_requests=1`; prefer startup configuration over per-request
      overrides; eliminate fatal errors and diagnostics on attacker-reachable
      paths
- [ ] Restart every PHP worker after any configuration change and confirm no
      pool, directory, or application setting restores a finite memory limit
      (CVE-2026-109618) or re-enables the features above (CVE-2026-109619)

## Correlation
- [ ] SHELL_SPAWN + TOOL_DOWNLOAD / NET_OUT / WEBSHELL_DROP on one host
      within 60 min → incident
- [ ] SHELL_SPAWN alone → suspicious; triage the command line, allowlist
      exact known application shell-outs
- [ ] WEBSHELL_DROP alone → incident candidate; forensic triage §5
- [ ] No §3 signals, host patched before exposure → close with the version
      evidence from §1

## Practice on the synthetic sample
From the repo root:

```bash
python3 07-kev-hunting/detect/php2shell-detect.py \
  07-kev-hunting/samples/php2shell-sysmon.log
```

Expect one `[INCIDENT]` (web-01: shell + download tool + outbound + webshell
drop inside 30 seconds) and three `[SUSPICIOUS]` (web-02: legitimate
application shell-out — `pdftotext`, triage to allowlist; web-03: lone shell
spawn; web-05: direct download-tool spawn under the worker). web-04 is clean:
FPM pool spawns, cron `php artisan`, admin and monitoring `curl`, a direct
outbound connection from the worker, and a template-cache `.php` write. All
lines are synthetic training data.

Wazuh: `07-kev-hunting/detect/php2shell-wazuh-rules.xml` — four rules
(100100 shell spawn, 100101 download tool, 100102 webshell drop, 100110
correlation). They were checked structurally only; there is no Wazuh manager
in this lab, so validate them on a manager before relying on them (see the
file header for the assumptions, including the stock Sysmon decoder fields
and the `negate` / `if_matched_group` points to confirm).
